# Museums and Cultural Places Near Us

Checked October 27, 2026. Within about an hour and a half of Santa Rosa. Each place links to its official site, with tags for what it holds.

## Sonoma County

- [California Indian Museum and Cultural Center](https://cimcc.org/), Santa Rosa. A Native-led museum telling California history from the perspective of more than 150 tribes, a strong fit for land-based learning about the first people of this place, open weekday afternoons with weekends by appointment. *Native, History.*
- [Santa Rosa Junior College Multicultural Museum (Jesse Peter Museum)](https://museum.santarosa.edu/), Santa Rosa. A small campus museum with Pomo baskets from the Elsie Allen collection and art from cultures around the world, open limited weekday hours with group visits by appointment. *Native, Art, History.*
- [Museum of Sonoma County](https://museumsc.org/), Santa Rosa. The county's art and history museum in the old post office, with rotating exhibits and Art4Kids and History4Kids programs, open Wednesday through Sunday. *Art, History.*
- [Children's Museum of Sonoma County](https://www.cmosc.org/visit/), Santa Rosa. A hands-on museum for children and caregivers exploring nature, science and art, with a pay-what-you-can Open Door Policy and free passes through the library. *Children, Science, Nature, Art.*
- [Charles M. Schulz Museum and Research Center](https://schulzmuseum.org/), Santa Rosa. The home of Peanuts art where children can see original comic strips and draw their own stories. *Art, Children.*
- [Luther Burbank Home and Gardens](https://lutherburbank.org/), Santa Rosa. The downtown gardens of the famous plant breeder, a living lesson in seeds, plants and patient observation, with no fee for the gardens. *Garden, History, Outdoors, Free.*
- [Environmental Discovery Center at Spring Lake](https://parks.sonomacounty.gov/visit/environmental-discovery-center), Santa Rosa. A county parks nature center with live animals and hands-on exhibits about local creeks and wildlife, right beside lake trails. *Nature, Science, Children, Outdoors.*
- [Petaluma Wildlife and Natural Science Museum](https://www.petalumawildlifemuseum.org/), Petaluma. A student-run natural history museum with live animals and specimens, open most Saturdays during the school year with children 4 and under free. *Nature, Science, Children.*
- [Sonoma Valley Museum of Art](https://svma.org/), Sonoma. A small art museum with rotating exhibits, free for visitors 18 and under and free for everyone on Wednesdays. *Art.*
- [Sonoma State Historic Park](https://parks.ca.gov/?lang=en&page_id=479), Sonoma. The mission, barracks and adobe buildings around the Sonoma Plaza, where children can walk thick adobe walls and courtyards. *History, Outdoors.*
- [Depot Park Museum](https://sonomavalleyhistory.org/), Sonoma. The Sonoma Valley Historical Society's small museum in a replica railroad depot near the bike path. *History.*
- [Petaluma Adobe State Historic Park](https://parks.ca.gov/?page_id=474), Petaluma. A huge 1830s adobe ranch building with open grounds, animals and seasonal living history days. *History, Outdoors.*
- [Tolay Lake Regional Park](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/tolay-lake-regional-park), Petaluma. A large park around a lake that is a sacred healing place for many California tribes, now cared for in partnership with the Federated Indians of Graton Rancheria. *Native, Nature, Outdoors.*
- [Jack London State Historic Park](https://jacklondonpark.com/), Glen Ellen. The writer's ranch with a small house museum, farm buildings, vineyards and oak woodland trails. *History, Nature, Outdoors.*
- [Sonoma Botanical Garden](https://sonomabg.org/), Glen Ellen. A large garden of wild-collected Asian plants with ponds, open woodland paths and seasonal family days. *Garden, Nature, Outdoors.*
- [Luther Burbank's Gold Ridge Experiment Farm](https://wschs.org/), Sebastopol. Burbank's historic test garden and cottage, with guided tours and garden walks led by the Western Sonoma County Historical Society. *Garden, History, Outdoors.*
- [West County Museum](https://wschs.org/museum/), Sebastopol. A small history museum in the old train depot, open weekend middays with free admission. *History, Free.*
- [Sebastopol Center for the Arts](https://www.sebarts.org/), Sebastopol. A community art center with galleries and classes that welcomes families. *Art.*
- [Healdsburg Museum and Historical Society](https://www.healdsburgmuseum.org/), Healdsburg. The town history museum with Pomo baskets and local history exhibits, temporarily closed October 26 to November 19, 2026 for a new installation. *History.*
- [Fort Ross State Historic Park](https://www.fortross.org/visitors), Jenner. A coastal fort and Kashaya Pomo homeland with a visitor center, reconstructed buildings and ocean bluffs. *History, Native, Outdoors.*
- [Armstrong Redwoods State Natural Reserve](https://www.parks.ca.gov/?page_id=450), Guerneville. An old-growth redwood grove with a visitor center and flat, stroller-friendly trails. *Nature, Outdoors.*
- [Bodega Marine Laboratory](https://marinescience.ucdavis.edu/events/public-tours-bodega-marine-laboratory), Bodega Bay. A UC Davis marine science station that offers scheduled public tours with tide pool animals and touch tanks. *Science, Nature.*
- [Pepperwood Preserve](https://www.pepperwoodpreserve.org/), Santa Rosa. A large nature preserve in Wappo homelands, open to the public only for scheduled guided hikes and family events. *Nature, Science, Outdoors.*
- [Pacific Coast Air Museum](https://www.pacificcoastairmuseum.org/), Santa Rosa. An outdoor collection of real airplanes and helicopters at the county airport, with open cockpit days when children can climb aboard. *History, Science, Outdoors.*
- [Petaluma Historical Library and Museum](https://cityofpetaluma.org/location/petaluma-historical-library-and-museum), Petaluma. The town history museum in the 1906 Carnegie library building, with a stained glass dome and local history exhibits. *History.*

## Marin County

- [Marin Museum of the American Indian](https://www.marinindian.com/visit), Novato. A Coast Miwok-centered museum in Miwok Park with hands-on exhibits and a native plant garden, free for children under 3 and for Native visitors, open Wednesday through Sunday. *Native, History, Children, Garden.*
- [Kule Loklo](https://www.nps.gov/places/point_reyes_kule_loklo.htm), Point Reyes Station. A replica Coast Miwok village with a roundhouse and kotchas a short walk from the Bear Valley Visitor Center. *Native, History, Outdoors.*
- [Bear Valley Visitor Center](https://www.nps.gov/pore/planyourvisit/hours.htm), Point Reyes Station. The main Point Reyes National Seashore visitor center with animal and habitat exhibits, near the Earthquake Trail. *Nature, Science, Outdoors.*
- [Olompali State Historic Park](https://www.parks.ca.gov/?page_id=465), Novato. A former Coast Miwok village site with a replica village, ranch ruins and oak hillside trails. *Native, History, Outdoors.*
- [Bay Area Discovery Museum](https://bayareadiscoverymuseum.org/plan-your-visit/), Sausalito. A children's museum built for ages 0 to 10, with indoor and outdoor play spaces under the Golden Gate Bridge. *Children, Science, Art, Outdoors.*
- [Bay Model Visitor Center](https://www.recreation.gov/gateways/1251), Sausalito. A giant working hydraulic model of the San Francisco Bay that children can walk around to see tides and water moving. *Science, Nature.*
- [The Marine Mammal Center](https://www.marinemammalcenter.org/education/adults-families/marine-science-sunday), Sausalito. A seal and sea lion hospital in the Marin Headlands where visitors can watch patients recover. *Science, Nature.*
- [China Camp State Park](https://www.parks.ca.gov/?page_id=466), San Rafael. A historic Chinese American shrimp fishing village with a small museum, a beach and shoreline trails. *Asian American, History, Nature, Outdoors.*
- [Angel Island Immigration Station](https://www.aiisf.org/plan-your-visit), Angel Island (ferry from Tiburon). The site where many Chinese and other Asian immigrants were held, with a museum and an island setting reached by ferry. *Asian American, History, Outdoors.*
- [Richardson Bay Audubon Center and Sanctuary](https://www.audubon.org/richardson-bay/visit), Tiburon. A bayfront bird sanctuary with a historic house and short trails for watching shorebirds. *Nature, Science, Outdoors.*
- [WildCare](https://discoverwildcare.org/), San Rafael. A wildlife hospital and nature education center now at an interim site, with its Wildlife Ambassador Zone temporarily closed. *Nature, Science.*
- [Marin History Museum at the Boyd Gate House](https://marinhistory.org/BoydGateHouse), San Rafael. The county history museum in an 1879 gatehouse, open Wednesday through Saturday. *History.*
- [Novato History Museum](https://www.novatohistory.org/novato), Novato. A small history museum in an 1850s house, open three afternoons a week. *History.*
- [Hamilton Field History Museum](https://www.novatohistory.org/novato), Novato. A small aviation museum about the old Army air base, open the same days as the Novato History Museum. *History.*
- [Marin Museum of Contemporary Art](https://marinmoca.org/visit), Novato. A contemporary art museum with artist studios in a former air base building. *Art.*
- [Marin Art and Garden Center](https://maringarden.org/), Ross. Historic gardens and art spaces with lawns, big trees and room to wander. *Garden, Art, Outdoors.*
- [Bolinas Museum](https://bolinasmuseum.org/visit), Bolinas. A coastal art and history museum, always free, open Friday through Sunday. *Art, History, Free.*
- [Jack Mason Museum of West Marin History](https://jackmasonmuseum.org/), Inverness. A tiny local history museum in a historic cottage with very limited hours. *History.*
- [Martin Griffin Preserve](https://www.allhandsecology.org/?p=1117), Stinson Beach. An All Hands Ecology preserve known for nesting herons and egrets, open only during scheduled events. *Nature, Outdoors.*
- [Point Reyes Lighthouse](https://www.nps.gov/pore/planyourvisit/lighthouse.htm), Inverness. A historic lighthouse at the tip of Point Reyes with an accessible visitor center and observation deck, though the 313 steps down to the lighthouse are best skipped with young children. *History, Nature, Outdoors.*
- [Muir Woods National Monument](https://www.nps.gov/muwo/planyourvisit/know-before-you-go.htm), Mill Valley. An old-growth redwood forest with flat boardwalk trails and a visitor center, with parking or shuttle reservations required. *Nature, Outdoors.*
- [Sausalito Historical Society Ice House Museum](https://www.sausalitohistoricalsociety.com/contact-and-hours), Sausalito. A small history museum and visitor center in an old ice house downtown, open Wednesday through Sunday. *History.*
- [Falkirk Cultural Center](https://cityofsanrafael.org/falkirk-art-galleries), San Rafael. A city-run Victorian mansion with art galleries and gardens, open weekday afternoons and Saturday mornings. *Art, History, Garden.*
- [Belvedere-Tiburon Landmarks Society Historic Sites](https://landmarkssociety.com/), Tiburon. The China Cabin, Old St. Hilary's on a wildflower hill and the Railroad and Ferry Depot Museum, small historic sites open seasonally. *History, Nature.*

## Napa County

- [di Rosa Center for Contemporary Art](https://www.dirosaart.org/), Napa. A large collection of Northern California art with outdoor sculpture, meadows and a lake. *Art, Outdoors.*
- [Napa County Historical Society](https://napahistory.org/plan-your-visit), Napa. Rotating local history exhibits in the historic Goodman Library downtown. *History.*
- [Napa Valley Museum Yountville](https://napavalleymuseum.org/visit/hours-admission), Yountville. An art and history museum for the valley, free for children 5 and under and open Thursday through Sunday. *Art, History.*
- [Bale Grist Mill State Historic Park](https://www.napavalleystateparks.org/bale-grist-mill-state-historic-park), St. Helena. A working water-powered mill where children can watch grain become flour on weekend tours. *History, Science, Outdoors.*
- [Bothe-Napa Valley State Park](https://www.parks.ca.gov/?lang=en&page_id=477), Calistoga. A redwood and oak park in Wappo homelands with a Native plant garden and creekside trails. *Nature, Native, Garden, Outdoors.*
- [Sharpsteen Museum](https://www.sharpsteenmuseum.org/), Calistoga. A history museum founded by a Disney animator, with a large hand-built diorama of early Calistoga. *History, Art.*
- [Robert Louis Stevenson Museum](https://stevensonmuseum.org/), St. Helena. A small museum about the author of A Child's Garden of Verses, open Tuesday through Saturday afternoons. *History, Art.*

## Solano County

- [Vallejo Naval and Historical Museum](https://vallejomuseum.org), Vallejo. The city and Mare Island shipyard history museum, which includes African American history exhibits, with children under 12 free. *History, African American.*
- [Mare Island Museum](https://www.mareislandhpf.org/museum.html), Vallejo. A shipyard history museum run by the Mare Island Historic Park Foundation, open weekdays and the first and third full weekends of each month, and home to a Filipinos on Mare Island exhibit. *History, Filipino.*
- [Museum of History Benicia](https://mohbenicia.org/), Benicia. The town history museum in the historic Benicia Arsenal buildings on Camel Road, open Friday and Saturday afternoons with free admission for all visitors. *History, Free.*
- [Benicia Capitol State Historic Park](https://www.parks.ca.gov/?page_id=475), Benicia. California's third state capitol building, a small brick building and garden where children can sit at old wooden desks. *History, Garden.*
- [Arts Benicia](https://artsbenicia.org), Benicia. A community art center with free exhibitions, Family Art Days and youth classes, open Thursday through Sunday afternoons during shows. *Art, Children, Free.*
- [Rush Ranch](https://solanolandtrust.org/protected-lands/rush-ranch/), Suisun City. A working ranch in the Suisun Marsh in Patwin homelands, with a blacksmith shop, barns and self-guided marsh trails open daily. *Nature, History, Native, Outdoors.*
- [Western Railway Museum](https://wrm.org/visit/plan-your-visit), Suisun City. A railway museum with historic streetcars that families can ride on weekends. *History, Science.*
- [Vacaville Museum](https://vacavillemuseum.org/visit/), Vacaville. The Center for Solano County History and Culture, with free admission and gallery hours Thursday through Saturday. *History, Free.*
- [Pena Adobe Historical Park](https://penaadobe.org/about), Vacaville. An 1840s adobe and small museum in a park with an Indian Council Ground, open the first Saturday of each month from February through December and for Kids Day events. *History, Native, Outdoors.*
- [Travis Heritage Center](https://www.travis.af.mil/Units/Heritage-Center/), Fairfield. An Air Force base museum with an outdoor airpark of big planes, free to visit, but visitors without a government ID must call ahead for base access. *History, Free, Outdoors.*

## Lake County

- [Anderson Marsh State Historic Park](https://andersonmarsh.org/), Lower Lake. A marsh and oak park holding Southeastern Pomo village sites and the Koi people's long history, with guided nature walks on the second Saturday of most months and ranch house tours after some walks. *Native, History, Nature, Outdoors.*
- [Clear Lake State Park](https://www.parks.ca.gov/?page_id=473), Kelseyville. A lakeside park with a visitor center about the area's natural and cultural history and the Indian Nature Trail through a former Pomo village site. *Nature, Native, Outdoors.*
- [Lake County Historic Courthouse Museum](https://www.lakecountyca.gov/Facilities/Facility/Details/Historic-Courthouse-Museum-1), Lakeport. The county history museum in the 1871 courthouse, holding one of the largest collections of Eastern Pomo baskets in the country, open Thursday through Saturday. *History, Native.*
- [Ely Stage Stop and Country Museum](https://lakecountyhistory.org/location-hours-map-ely-stage-stop), Kelseyville. A restored stagecoach stop with barns and farm equipment, open weekend middays. *History, Outdoors.*
- [Middletown Art Center](http://www.middletownartcenter.org/index.html), Middletown. A community arts hub with exhibitions, classes and workshops featuring local and regional artists. *Art.*
- [Taylor Observatory](https://www.lakecoe.org/edservices/observatory), Kelseyville. A Lake County Office of Education observatory open to the public only during scheduled evening sky events. *Science, Nature.*

## Mendocino County

- [Grace Hudson Museum and Sun House](https://gracehudsonmuseum.org/visit), Ukiah. A museum of Pomo baskets and Grace Hudson's paintings of Pomo children, with a historic redwood home and gardens, free for Native visitors and free for everyone on first Fridays. *Native, Art, History, Garden.*
- [City of Ten Thousand Buddhas](https://cttbusa.org/), Talmage. A large Buddhist monastery and community with gardens, peacocks and temple halls, open to visitors daily. *Asian American, Garden, Outdoors.*
- [Mendocino County Museum](https://www.mendocinocounty.gov/departments/museum/visit), Willits. The county museum of history and natural history, free on the first Saturday of each month and for children under 5. *History, Nature, Native.*
- [Roots of Motive Power](https://rootsofmotivepower.com/), Willits. A collection of steam engines, logging equipment and trains next to the county museum, free to tour on the first and third Saturdays of the month. *History, Science, Free.*
- [Anderson Valley Historical Museum](https://www.andersonvalleymuseum.org), Boonville. A one-room little red schoolhouse museum open weekend afternoons from February through November. *History.*

## San Francisco

San Francisco is about an hour from Santa Rosa. Places are grouped by kind, and the ones marked free name who gets in free.

### Art

- [de Young Museum](https://www.famsf.org/visit/de-young-tickets-hours), Golden Gate Park. A large art museum with art from Africa, Oceania and the Americas, and an observation tower where children can look out over the park canopy, and its Oceanic gallery shows Samoan siapo (tapa cloth) and fine mats. *Art, Native, Pacific Islander, Free (youth 17 and under).*
- [Legion of Honor](https://www.famsf.org/learn-engage/kids-families), Lincoln Park (Outer Richmond). A fine arts museum on a clifftop above the Golden Gate, with sculpture courtyards and ocean views that pair well with a walk at nearby Lands End. *Art, History.*
- [Asian Art Museum](https://about.asianart.org/plan-your-visit/), Civic Center. One of the largest collections of Asian art in the country, with general admission free on the first Sunday of each month and rich material on animals, textiles and clay. *Art, Asian American.*
- [SFMOMA (San Francisco Museum of Modern Art)](https://www.sfmoma.org/for-families/), SoMa. A modern art museum with family programs and free ground and second floor artworks that need no ticket, good for short looking visits with small children. *Art, Children, Free (18 and under).*
- [Museum of the African Diaspora (MoAD)](https://www.moadsf.org/visit), SoMa / Yerba Buena. A contemporary museum of art and culture from across the African diaspora, with free community days on second Saturdays. *Art, African American, Free (children 12 and under).*
- [Yerba Buena Center for the Arts (YBCA)](https://ybca.org/visit/), SoMa / Yerba Buena. A contemporary arts center with changing exhibitions often made by Bay Area BIPOC artists, and galleries free to all on Wednesdays. *Art, Free (youth 17 and under).*
- [Museum of Craft and Design](https://sfmcd.org/visit/), Dogpatch. A small museum of handmade objects and design with hands-on MakeArt workshops and free children's group tours for groups of 15 or more. *Art, Children, Free (children through age 12).*
- [Children's Creativity Museum](https://creativity.org/hours-admission/), SoMa / Yerba Buena. A hands-on art and technology museum for children ages 2 to 12, open Wednesday to Sunday. *Art, Children.*
- [African American Art and Culture Complex](http://aaacc.org/), Western Addition (Fillmore). A Black arts center with a gallery, theater and community garden group under one roof, rooted in the Fillmore's African American history. *Art, African American.*
- [Ruth Williams Opera House (formerly Bayview Opera House)](https://rwoh.org/), Bayview Hunters Point. A historic theater that serves as Bayview's performing arts and cultural center, with community festivals such as the Afro Latinx Festival. *Art, African American, Latino.*
- [Precita Eyes Muralists Visitor Center](https://www.precitaeyes.org/about.html), Mission. A community mural arts center that offers Toddler Kids art classes, school tours and family friendly mural walks through the Mission. *Art, Latino, Children.*
- [Galería de la Raza](https://galeriadelaraza.org/), Mission. A Chicano and Latino arts organization whose Studio 24 education annex on Folsom Street is open Tuesday to Friday, while its main 16th Street gallery is under construction. *Art, Latino.*
- [Mission Cultural Center for Latino Arts](http://www.missionculturalcenter.org/), Mission. A Latino arts and culture center known for printmaking, dance and Día de los Muertos events, temporarily closed since January 2026 while it relocates from its 2868 Mission Street building. *Art, Latino.*
- [The Mexican Museum](https://mexicanmuseum.org/), SoMa / Yerba Buena. A collection of Mexican, Chicano and Latino art that is not currently open to visitors while it prepares to move into a permanent home at 706 Mission Street. *Art, Latino.*
- [Chinese Culture Center of San Francisco](https://www.cccsf.us/60-af), Chinatown. A Chinese American arts center with a new street level gallery at 667 Grant Avenue that hosts free community open houses and kid friendly art activities. *Art, Asian American.*
- [SOMArts Cultural Center](https://somarts.org/visit-us/), SoMa. A community gallery that hosts the city's large annual Día de los Muertos altar exhibition each fall, open Thursday to Sunday. *Art, Latino.*
- [Coit Tower](https://sfrecpark.org/facilities/facility/details/Coit-Tower-290), Telegraph Hill. A hilltop tower whose ground floor is wrapped in 1930s WPA murals of California farms, docks and city life, with an elevator to the top that is free for small children. *Art, History, Free (elevator for children 4 and under).*
- [Beach Chalet Visitors Center](https://www.beachchalet.com/visitors-center), Golden Gate Park (Ocean Beach). The first floor of the Beach Chalet building holds Lucien Labaudt's 1936 frescos of San Francisco life, open during restaurant hours, so call ahead to confirm access. *Art, History.*
- [Acción Latina Juan R. Fuentes Gallery](https://accionlatina.org/en/art-gallery/), Mission. A Latino community arts gallery on 24th Street that hosts exhibitions and the free bilingual Paseo Artístico arts walk, with gallery hours not posted, so check the calendar first. *Art, Latino.*
- [Bindlestiff Studio](https://www.bindlestiffstudio.org/), SoMa. A small theater known as the home of Filipino American performing arts, where most shows are evenings, so look for weekend matinees and youth programs. *Art, Filipino.*
- [Museo Italo Americano](https://sfmuseo.org/), Marina (Fort Mason Center). A small museum of Italian and Italian American art in Fort Mason's Building C, with gallery hours not posted, so check before visiting. *Art, History.*

### History and culture

- [Chinese Historical Society of America Museum](https://chsa.org/), Chinatown. The oldest organization in the country devoted to Chinese American history, housed in the historic Julia Morgan designed Chinatown YWCA building. *History, Asian American.*
- [Manilatown Heritage Foundation (International Hotel Manilatown Center)](https://manilatown.org/international-hotel-manilatown-center), Chinatown / Manilatown. A community museum and gathering space at the rebuilt I-Hotel that tells the story of Filipino elders and Manilatown, with gallery hours Wednesday to Sunday afternoons. *History, Filipino, Asian American.*
- [Japanese Cultural and Community Center of Northern California (JCCCNC)](http://www.jcccnc.org), Japantown. A Japanese American community center that hosts family events such as the Halloween Carnival and Kodomo no Hi children's day, plus hands-on food workshops like onigiri and miso making. *History, Asian American, Children.*
- [San Francisco Public Library Filipino American Center](https://sfpl.org/locations/main-library/filipino-american-center), Civic Center. A third floor collection at the Main Library centered on the Filipino American experience, with books in English, Filipino and other Philippine languages. *History, Filipino.*
- [San Francisco Public Library African American Center and Chinese Center](https://sfpl.org/locations/main-library), Civic Center. Two community collections on the third floor of the Main Library that support family research and culturally grounded read-alouds. *History, African American, Asian American.*
- [American Indian Cultural Center](https://www.aiccsf.org/), Mission. A Native-led cultural organization that partners on public art and community events in the American Indian Cultural District, with no regular public venue hours confirmed, so check its events first. *History, Native.*
- [Asian Pacific Islander Cultural Center (APICC) and KULARTS](https://www.apiculturalcenter.org/building), SoMa. One of the city's official cultural centers, presenting Asian and Pacific Islander arts and festivals, which with the Filipino arts group KULARTS is building a new performance and gallery space at 262 7th Street that is not open yet, so check events first. *Art, Asian American, Pacific Islander, Filipino.*
- [Mission Dolores (Mission San Francisco de Asís)](https://www.missiondolores.org/old-mission), Mission. The city's oldest building, where the cemetery is the resting place of some 5,000 Ohlone, Miwok and other First Californians and the garden includes an Ohlone ethnobotanic planting. *History, Native, Garden.*
- [Cable Car Museum](https://www.cablecarmuseum.org/info.html), Nob Hill. A working powerhouse where children can watch the giant wheels that pull the cable cars, open Tuesday to Sunday. *History, Science, Children, Free.*
- [Musée Mécanique](https://museemecanique.com), Fisherman's Wharf (Pier 45). A collection of antique mechanical arcade machines and automata where children can see gears, music boxes and moving figures up close, with entry free and each machine paid per play. *History, Children.*
- [Walt Disney Family Museum](https://www.waltdisney.org/visit/admission), Presidio. A museum of animation history with sketches, early drawings and studio stories that invite children to think about how pictures come to move. *Art, History, Free (children 5 and under).*
- [Fort Point National Historic Site](https://www.nps.gov/fopo/planyourvisit/index.htm), Presidio. A Civil War era brick fort beneath the Golden Gate Bridge, open Thursday to Monday, with waves, wind and the bridge overhead. *History, Outdoors.*
- [San Francisco Maritime National Historical Park](https://www.nps.gov/safr/index.htm), Fisherman's Wharf / Aquatic Park. A national park about ships and the bay, but note that Hyde Street Pier is closed for renovation and its historic ships have moved to Mare Island. *History, Outdoors.*
- [GLBT Historical Society Museum](https://www.glbthistory.org/museum-about-visitor-info), Castro. A small museum of LGBTQ history designed mainly for adults, better suited to educators and families with older children. *History, Free (children 12 and under).*
- [Contemporary Jewish Museum](https://thecjm.org/pages/658), SoMa / Yerba Buena. A museum of Jewish art and culture that is temporarily closed to the public while it sells its building and plans programs with partner organizations. *Art, History.*
- [NJAHS Japantown Peace Gallery](https://www.njahs.org/japantown-peace-gallery/), Japantown. A free gallery of the National Japanese American Historical Society with changing exhibits on Japanese American life, open weekday afternoons and the first Saturday of each month. *History, Asian American, Free.*
- [Pacific Islander Cultural District](https://www.apiculturalcenter.org/event-details/pacific-islander-cultural-district-inaugural-celebration), Visitacion Valley. A city cultural district honoring Samoan, Tongan and other Pacific Islander communities, with no visitor venue, so watch for its community festival and procession. *History, Pacific Islander.*
- [Presidio Officers' Club Heritage Gallery](https://presidio.gov/explore/attractions/presidio-officers-club), Presidio. Free history exhibitions that trace the site from its Indigenous past through its years as an army post, open Friday to Sunday. *History, Native, Free.*
- [Presidio Visitor Center](https://presidio.gov/explore/attractions/presidio-visitor-center), Presidio. A visitor center open daily with a large 3D model of the Presidio, touch screens and before and after views of habitat restoration, a short walk from Tunnel Tops. *History, Nature, Children.*
- [San Francisco Railway Museum](https://www.streetcar.org/museum/), Embarcadero. A small streetcar museum across from the Ferry Building, open Tuesday to Saturday afternoons, where children can watch vintage streetcars roll past on the F line. *History, Children, Free.*
- [San Francisco Fire Department Museum](https://guardiansofthecity.org/sffd/), Laurel Heights (Presidio Avenue). A volunteer run museum of old fire engines and gear, open Thursday to Sunday afternoons as staffing permits, so call ahead the day of your visit. *History, Children, Free.*

### Children, science and nature

- [Exploratorium](https://www.exploratorium.edu/visit), Embarcadero (Pier 15). A hands-on museum of science, art and perception with hundreds of touchable exhibits that invite children to test and wonder. *Science, Children, Free (children 3 and under).*
- [California Academy of Sciences](https://www.calacademy.org/), Golden Gate Park. An aquarium, rainforest dome, natural history museum and living roof under one roof, with African penguins young children love. *Science, Nature, Children, Free (children 2 and under).*
- [Randall Museum](https://randallmuseum.org/), Corona Heights. A small city museum of science, nature and art with live animal ambassadors, drop-in activities and Saturday Science, set beside Corona Heights Park. *Science, Nature, Children, Free.*
- [Presidio Field Station](https://presidio.gov/explore/attractions/field-station), Presidio Tunnel Tops. A free curiosity lab with nature specimens, artifacts and maps to explore with the senses, plus loaner binoculars, magnifiers and a Presidio Explorer Backpack. *Nature, Science, Children, Free.*
- [San Francisco Botanical Garden](https://gggp.org/san-francisco-botanical-garden/), Golden Gate Park. A 55 acre garden of plants from many climates, with free early morning hours and free second Tuesdays. *Garden, Nature, Outdoors, Free (children 4 and under and SF residents).*
- [Conservatory of Flowers](https://gggp.org/conservatory-of-flowers/), Golden Gate Park. A Victorian glass greenhouse full of tropical plants, water lilies and orchids, free for San Francisco residents. *Garden, Nature, History.*
- [Japanese Tea Garden](https://gggp.org/japanese-tea-garden/), Golden Gate Park. The oldest public Japanese garden in the country, with koi ponds, a drum bridge and a pagoda, free for San Francisco residents. *Garden, Asian American, History, Outdoors.*
- [San Francisco Zoo and Gardens](https://www.sfzoo.org/tickets-hours/), Lakeshore (near Ocean Beach). A large zoo open every day of the year where children can watch animals from many habitats. *Nature, Science, Children, Free (children under 2).*
- [Aquarium of the Bay](https://www.aquariumofthebay.org/tickets/), Fisherman's Wharf (Pier 39). A small aquarium focused on the animals of San Francisco Bay, including river otters, with walk-through tunnels under the water. *Nature, Science, Children.*
- [Alemany Farm](https://sfrecpark.org/1068/Alemany-Farm), Bernal Heights (Alemany Boulevard). A 3.5 acre community food farm where volunteers grow and share produce, with workdays on Monday and Saturday afternoons and teaching in beekeeping and pollinator gardens. *Garden, Nature, Outdoors.*
- [Garden for the Environment](https://www.gardenfortheenvironment.org/garden), Inner Sunset (7th Avenue). A demonstration garden for organic and native plant gardening, open every day from dawn to dusk, with youth field trips and a self-guided tour. *Garden, Nature, Outdoors.*

### Outdoors and public art

- [Andy Goldsworthy's Spire](https://presidio.gov/explore/attractions/andy-goldsworthys-spire), Presidio. A tall spire made from the trunks of cypress trees, set in a young forest that has been growing up around it. *Art, Nature, Outdoors, Free.*
- [Andy Goldsworthy's Wood Line](https://presidio.gov/explore/attractions/andy-goldsworthys-wood-line), Presidio. A long, low line of eucalyptus branches that snakes along the forest floor among tall trees, an easy walk for small legs. *Art, Nature, Outdoors, Free.*
- [Andy Goldsworthy's Tree Fall and Earth Wall](https://presidio.gov/goldsworthy-in-the-presidio), Presidio. Two more Goldsworthy works made from Presidio trees and earth, though the Presidio lists Tree Fall as not currently open for public visits. *Art, Nature.*
- [Presidio Tunnel Tops and Outpost Playground](https://presidio.gov/explore/attractions/outpost-playground), Presidio. A park over the highway with a free nature play area built from logs and boulders, plus picnic canopies by artists Favianna Rodriguez, Felicia Gabaldon and Tosha Stimage. *Outdoors, Children, Art, Free.*
- [Mission murals and Balmy Alley](https://www.precitaeyes.org/tours), Mission. Walls of painted figures, flowers and community stories along a brick lane, best seen on a Precita Eyes guided mural walk or on your own. *Art, Latino, Outdoors.*
- [American Indian Cultural District](https://americanindianculturaldistrict.org), Mission. A city cultural district on unceded Ramaytush Ohlone land in Yelamu, with Native-led public art, sculptures and community events. *Native, Art, Outdoors.*
- [SOMA Pilipinas Filipino Cultural Heritage District](https://somapilipinas.org/our-district), SoMa. A walkable district of Filipino murals, the Mahal Jeepney and Victoria Manalo Draves Park, plus groups such as Bindlestiff Studio and Kularts. *Filipino, Art, Outdoors.*
- [Yerba Buena Gardens](https://yerbabuenagardens.org/), SoMa / Yerba Buena. Downtown public gardens with lawns and public art, next door to MoAD, YBCA and the Children's Creativity Museum. *Garden, Art, Outdoors.*
- [Japantown Peace Plaza and Peace Pagoda](https://www.sf.gov/news/city-officials-and-japantown-community-break-ground-peace-plaza-renovation-project), Japantown. The plaza around the five tiered Peace Pagoda, a gift from Osaka, is closed for a renovation the city expected to finish in summer or fall 2026, so check whether it has reopened. *History, Asian American, Outdoors.*
- [Victoria Manalo Draves Park](https://sfrecpark.org/Facilities/Facility/Details/Victoria-Manalo-Draves-Park-386), SoMa. A neighborhood park with a playground and community garden named for the Filipina American diver who grew up in SoMa and won two Olympic golds in 1948, with a plaque telling her story. *Filipino, Outdoors, Children.*
- [MaestraPeace Mural at the Women's Building](https://www.womensbuilding.org/our-building/the-mural), Mission. A five story mural painted by seven women muralists that honors women and cultural figures from around the world, seen from 18th and Lapidge Streets. *Art, Latino, Outdoors.*
- [Clarion Alley Murals](https://clarionalleymuralproject.org/tours/), Mission. An alley of ever changing murals between Valencia and Mission Streets, with artist-led tours, though some murals carry strong political messages, so preview it first. *Art, Outdoors, Free (tours for children under 12).*
- [Lands End Lookout and Sutro Baths](https://www.nps.gov/places/000/lands-end-lookout-visitor-center.htm), Outer Richmond. A visitor center open daily with history and geology exhibits, beside coastal trails and the ruins of the old Sutro Baths, where cliffs mean small children need a close hand. *History, Nature, Outdoors.*
- [PIER 39 Sea Lions](https://www.pier39.com/sealions/), Fisherman's Wharf. California sea lions haul out on the K-Dock floats, where children can watch, listen and count them, or watch the live webcam before a trip. *Nature, Outdoors.*

## The East Bay

- [African American Museum and Library at Oakland (AAMLO)](https://oaklandlibrary.org/aamlo), Oakland. A library and museum of Black history in Northern California, with a free-to-walk-in exhibit hall and a monthly AAMLO Kids Club and Festival of Black Dolls that welcome young children and families. *African American, History.*
- [Black Panther Party Museum](https://hueypnewtonfoundation.org/black-panther-party-museum), Oakland. A small downtown museum from the Dr. Huey P. Newton Foundation that tells the Party's community story, including its free breakfast program and the Oakland Community School, best for educators and families with grown-up guidance, open Wednesday to Saturday 10 am to 3 pm and Monday or Tuesday by appointment. *African American, History.*
- [Oakland Museum of California (OMCA)](https://museumca.org), Oakland. One museum for California art, history and natural sciences, with hands-on galleries, live-animal and habitat displays and terraced gardens where small children can roam. *Art, History, Science, Nature, Garden, Outdoors, Free (children 12 and under).*
- [Chabot Space and Science Center](https://chabotspace.org), Oakland. A hilltop science center in the redwoods with telescopes, a planetarium and hands-on space exhibits, and listed hours differ between sources, so check days open before visiting. *Science, Nature.*
- [Lawrence Hall of Science](https://www.lawrencehallofscience.org), Berkeley. UC Berkeley's public science center, with an Animal Discovery Zone, an outdoor Nature Lab for climbing and crawling, and water and erosion tables suited to children two and up. *Science, Nature, Children, Outdoors, Free (children 2 and under).*
- [Phoebe A. Hearst Museum of Anthropology](https://hearstmuseum.berkeley.edu/visit/), Berkeley. A university anthropology museum holding one of the largest collections of California Native baskets and belongings, good for educator research and small family visits, with limited public hours of Fridays noon to 4 pm. *Native, History.*
- [UC Botanical Garden at Berkeley](https://botanicalgarden.berkeley.edu/visit), Berkeley. A 34-acre garden in Strawberry Canyon with plants from around the world, a redwood grove and glass houses that invite slow, sensory exploration, closed Tuesdays. *Garden, Nature, Science, Outdoors, Free (children 4 and under).*
- [Berkeley Art Museum and Pacific Film Archive (BAMPFA)](https://bampfa.org/visit/hours), Berkeley. The university's art museum, with drop-in art studios for families and a light-filled building good for looking closely at art together. *Art, Free (children 13 and under).*
- [Habitot Children's Museum](https://habitot.org), Berkeley. An early childhood museum built around play, currently 100 percent mobile with pop-up visits at libraries and community sites instead of a permanent building, so check its locations and dates page. *Children.*
- [Shorebird Park Nature Center](https://www.berkeleyca.gov/community-recreation/waterfront/shorebird-nature-center), Berkeley. A small bayside nature center at the Berkeley Marina with tanks of local sea life and low-tide walks, open Tuesday to Saturday 9 am to 5 pm. *Nature, Science, Outdoors.*
- [Berkeley Art Center](https://berkeleyartcenter.org/visit), Berkeley. A community gallery in Live Oak Park beside a creek, a calm place to see local artists' work, open Thursday to Sunday noon to 5 pm with closures in late August and late November. *Art, Free, Outdoors.*
- [La Peña Cultural Center](https://lapena.org), Berkeley. A South Berkeley cultural center founded in 1975 by the Latin American community, with music, murals and family celebrations such as Día de Muertos, so check its calendar for daytime family events. *Latino, Art.*
- [Tilden Nature Area and Little Farm](https://www.ebparks.org/maps/tilden-nature-area), Berkeley. A free working farm with cows, goats, sheep and chickens next to the Environmental Education Center and nature trails, a near-perfect fit for a nature-based preschool, though public feeding of the animals ended in spring 2026. *Nature, Outdoors, Free.*
- [Regional Parks Botanic Garden](https://www.ebparks.org/parks/tilden/botanic-garden), Berkeley. A garden in Tilden Park devoted entirely to California native plants, arranged by region along a creek, open daily with no entrance or parking fee. *Garden, Nature, Outdoors, Free.*
- [Children's Fairyland](https://fairyland.org), Oakland. A storybook park on Lake Merritt designed for children under eight, with small play sets, puppet shows and animals, open Wednesday to Sunday 10 am to 4 pm, weather permitting. *Children, Outdoors, Free (under age 1).*
- [Rotary Nature Center](https://www.oaklandca.gov/Community/Parks-Facilities/Recreation-Centers/Rotary-Natural-Science-Center), Oakland. A small nature center at Lake Merritt, North America's first official wildlife refuge, where children can watch waterbirds and learn about the lake, open Tuesday to Saturday 11 am to 5 pm. *Nature, Science, Outdoors.*
- [The Gardens at Lake Merritt](https://gardensatlakemerritt.org/), Oakland. A group of volunteer-run gardens in Lakeside Park, including a Japanese garden, bonsai garden, sensory garden, edible gardens and a pollinator garden, open daily. *Garden, Nature, Outdoors, Free.*
- [Oakland Zoo](https://oaklandzoo.org/admission), Oakland. A large hillside zoo focused on conservation, with native California wildlife trails and a children's petting area, useful for long looking at real animals. *Nature, Outdoors.*
- [Peralta Hacienda Historical Park](https://www.peraltahacienda.org/VisitUs.htm), Oakland. A Fruitvale park on the site of the Peralta family rancho that tells the layered stories of Ohlone, Californio, Mexican and immigrant families through outdoor exhibits, a native plant garden and history-themed play structures, open year round. *History, Latino, Native, Garden, Outdoors.*
- [Oakland Asian Cultural Center (OACC)](http://www.oacc.cc/programs/exhibitions.html), Oakland. A Chinatown cultural center with free exhibitions, classes and a large Lunar New Year celebration, sharing Asian and Pacific Islander arts and traditions, with some weekday morning visits by appointment only. *Asian American, Pacific Islander, Art.*
- [Intertribal Friendship House](https://www.ifhurbanrez.org), Oakland. One of the oldest urban American Indian community centers in the country, hosting public gatherings such as a California Native Spring Festival and gardening day that families can join, so plan around its event calendar. *Native.*
- [Sogorea Te' Land Trust](https://sogoreate-landtrust.org/public-education/), Oakland. An urban Indigenous women-led land trust returning Lisjan (Ohlone) land to Indigenous stewardship, offering speakers for schools by request (one month ahead) and community work days and cultural events at its land sites. *Native, Outdoors.*
- [EastSide Cultural Center](https://eastsideartsalliance.org/eastside-cultural-center), Oakland. A community arts center and gallery on International Boulevard run by EastSide Arts Alliance, rooted in East Oakland's communities of color, with public hours not posted, so check its calendar for open events. *Art.*
- [Crab Cove Visitor Center](https://www.ebparks.org/parks/visitor-centers/crab-cove), Alameda. A small marine center at Crown Beach with an 800-gallon bay aquarium and tidepool-style displays, ideal before a walk on the sand, open Wednesday to Sunday with a $5 parking fee. *Nature, Science, Outdoors.*
- [Rosie the Riveter WWII Home Front National Historical Park](https://home.nps.gov/rori), Richmond. A national park visitor center on the Richmond waterfront telling the stories of the women, families and workers of color who built ships in World War II, open daily 10 am to 5 pm. *History, Outdoors, Free.*
- [Richmond Art Center](https://richmondartcenter.org), Richmond. A community art center with galleries open to the public and studio classes, a friendly first art museum visit, open Tuesday to Saturday 11 am to 5 pm. *Art, Free.*
- [Richmond Museum of History and Culture](https://richmondmuseum.org/visit), Richmond. A small city history museum with pay-what-you-can admission, open Thursday to Sunday 1 to 4 pm. *History.*
- [Lindsay Wildlife Experience](https://lindsaywildlife.org), Walnut Creek. A wildlife hospital and museum where children meet non-releasable native animals such as owls, hawks and foxes up close. *Nature, Science, Children.*
- [Ruth Bancroft Garden](https://www.ruthbancroftgarden.org/visit/), Walnut Creek. A world-known dry garden of cacti, succulents and drought-tolerant plants with striking shapes and textures, open Wednesday to Sunday 9 am to 4 pm. *Garden, Nature, Outdoors, Free (children 4 and under).*
- [Bedford Gallery](https://www.bedfordgallery.org/about/visit), Walnut Creek. A contemporary art gallery inside the Lesher Center for the Arts with changing exhibitions and pay-what-you-can admission, open Wednesday to Sunday noon to 5 pm. *Art.*
- [Markham Nature Park and Arboretum](https://markhamarboretum.org/), Concord. A volunteer-tended arboretum along a creek with gardens of plants from around the world and a native plant area, with hours to confirm before a group visit. *Garden, Nature, Outdoors.*
- [John Muir National Historic Site](https://www.nps.gov/jomu/planyourvisit/index.htm), Martinez. The naturalist John Muir's home and fruit orchard, with grounds, trails and a visitor center that suit a nature-based school well, with no entrance fee. *History, Nature, Outdoors, Free.*
- [Sulphur Creek Nature Center](https://www.haywardrec.org/), Hayward. A small wildlife center in a creek canyon with live native animals and an animal lending library, open Tuesday to Sunday 10 am to 5 pm. *Nature, Science, Outdoors.*
- [Hayward Japanese Gardens](https://www.haywardrec.org/), Hayward. A traditional-style Japanese garden of stone, water, koi and pruned pines, open daily 8:30 am to 4 pm, and listings say entry is free. *Garden, Asian American, Outdoors.*
- [HAHS Museum of History and Culture](https://haywardareahistory.org/hahs-museum-of-history-culture), Hayward. The Hayward Area Historical Society's downtown museum, with local history exhibits and family days such as Día de los Muertos story time, open Tuesday to Saturday 11 am to 4 pm. *History.*
- [Coyote Hills Regional Park](https://ebparks.org/maps/coyote-hills), Fremont. A bayside park with an Ohlone shellmound village site, a visitor center with exhibits on Ohlone peoples and an annual Gathering of Ohlone Peoples, plus marsh boardwalks for bird watching, with village site tours offered as scheduled programs. *Native, History, Nature, Outdoors.*
- [Ardenwood Historic Farm](https://ebparks.org/parks/ardenwood), Fremont. A working 1880s-era farm park with farm animals, heirloom crops, a Victorian farmhouse and seasonal events such as sheep shearing and cider pressing, open Tuesday to Sunday 10 am to 4 pm, with some buildings possibly closed for construction through November 25, 2026. *History, Nature, Garden, Outdoors, Free (children under 4).*
- [Don Edwards San Francisco Bay National Wildlife Refuge](https://www.fws.gov/refuge/don-edwards-san-francisco-bay/visit-us), Fremont. A national wildlife refuge on the bay's salt marshes with a visitor center and easy trails for spotting shorebirds, with the Fremont visitor center open weekends 10 am to 2 pm. *Nature, Outdoors.*
- [Children's Natural History Museum](https://cnhm.msnucleus.org/), Fremont. A small, hands-on museum of rocks, fossils, shells and animals run by a science education nonprofit, with short open hours and a note that it is not recommended for children under 4, so it suits the older preschool group. *Science, Nature, Children.*
- [Old Mission San José](https://missionsanjose.org), Fremont. The restored 1797 mission church and museum, a site that holds both Spanish colonial history and the Ohlone people's story, with current hours to confirm because the official site is mid-transition. *History, Native, Latino.*

## The Peninsula

- [CuriOdyssey](https://curiodyssey.org/visit/), San Mateo. A small science and wildlife center at Coyote Point with native animals such as otters and owls, hands-on exhibits and a Nature Play Grove. *Science, Nature, Children, Outdoors, Free (infants 0 to 17 months).*
- [Central Park Japanese Garden](https://cityofsanmateo.org/3319/Central-Park-Japanese-Garden), San Mateo. A traditional Japanese garden with a koi pond and tea house in downtown Central Park, a quiet place for slow looking, open daily. *Garden, Asian American, Outdoors.*
- [Bay Area Aloha Festival](https://www.pica-org.org/about-pica), San Mateo. An annual summer weekend of Pacific Islander dance, music, crafts and food at the San Mateo County Event Center, put on by the Pacific Islanders' Cultural Association, an event and not a year-round site. *Pacific Islander.*
- [Hiller Aviation Museum](https://hiller.org/visit/), San Carlos. An aviation museum with real aircraft, helicopters and kid-height cockpits next to the San Carlos airport, open daily 10 am to 5 pm. *Science, History, Free (children 3 and under).*
- [San Mateo County History Museum](https://historysmc.org), Redwood City. The county history museum in the domed 1910 courthouse, with a regular preschool program of a story and craft, and the museum says admission is free. *History, Free.*
- [Cantor Arts Center](https://museum.stanford.edu/visit), Stanford. Stanford's large art museum with collections from around the world and the outdoor Rodin sculpture garden, always free, closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays. *Art, Outdoors, Free.*
- [Anderson Collection at Stanford](https://anderson.stanford.edu), Stanford. A museum of modern and contemporary American art with bold, large paintings that spark conversation, always free with no reservation, open Thursday to Monday 11 am to 5 pm. *Art, Free.*
- [Arizona Cactus Garden](https://facops.stanford.edu/arizona-garden), Stanford. A historic 1880s cactus and succulent garden near the Stanford mausoleum, a striking place to compare plant shapes and textures, with public access hours to confirm. *Garden, Nature, Outdoors.*
- [Palo Alto Junior Museum and Zoo](https://www.paloaltozoo.org/Visit), Palo Alto. A science museum and small zoo built for young children, with hands-on exhibits and a netted loose-animal habitat, open Tuesday to Sunday with timed entry. *Science, Nature, Children, Free (children under 12 months).*
- [Palo Alto Art Center](https://www.paloalto.gov/Departments/Community-Services/Arts-Sciences/Palo-Alto-Art-Center/Make-Art/Creative-Space), Palo Alto. A city art center with exhibitions, Family Days and a free drop-in Creative Space and Reading Lounge for hands-on art and children's books. *Art, Children.*
- [Museum of American Heritage](https://www.moah.org/visit), Palo Alto. A small museum of everyday machines and inventions in a historic house, with tinkering appeal for curious children, open Friday to Sunday 11 am to 4 pm. *History, Science, Free.*
- [Elizabeth F. Gamble Garden](https://gamblegarden.org/visit-us), Palo Alto. A historic house and garden with flower beds, an orchard and seasonal family events such as an apple celebration, open every day in daylight hours. *Garden, History, Outdoors, Free.*
- [Lucy Evans Baylands Nature Interpretive Center](https://www.paloalto.gov/Departments/Community-Services/Facility-Rentals/Nature-Interpretive-Centers/Baylands-Nature-Interpretive-Center), Palo Alto. A small nature center on stilts at the edge of a salt marsh, with a boardwalk out over the wetland for watching shorebirds, open weekends only (Saturday noon to 3 pm and Sunday 10 am to 3 pm per listings), so confirm before going. *Nature, Science, Outdoors.*
- [Filoli Historic House and Garden](https://filoli.org), Woodside. A historic estate with 16 acres of formal gardens, an orchard and nature trails, rich for seasonal noticing of blooms, fruit and birds, with hours and ticket prices to confirm on its site. *Garden, History, Nature, Outdoors.*
